renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: top_expressed_genes_heatmap
  title: Most expressed genes by sample
  description: |-
    Each cell is the Bambu read count of one of the most highly counted genes (rows) in one sample (columns), scaled per gene, with the gene biotype as a row annotation. It answers whether the highest-count genes behave the same in every library.
    How to read: columns of the same condition should share a pattern. A sample that looks unlike its replicates, or a block of genes high in one condition only, shows the main expression differences before any statistics. Colour is a per-gene z-score, so it shows the pattern across samples and not the absolute level.
    Lines and annotations: the genes are the 50 with the highest total count across samples, a fixed display size of this catalog's recipe and not a significance cut-off. Counts are Bambu's estimated gene counts.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoekeLab/bambu/master/README.md
  kind: complex_heatmap
  config:
    normalize: row_z
  roles:
    index: gene_id
    row_annotation_cols:
    - gene_biotype

- component: card
  id: top_biotypes
  title: Dominant gene biotype
  description: |-
    The hero number is the most frequent biotype among the displayed genes, the compact line gives how many biotypes occur, and the bars rank them by gene count. It answers what kind of genes take the most reads.
    How to read: protein-coding genes usually dominate. A large share of mitochondrial or ribosomal RNA among the top genes points to a library with little mRNA enrichment.
  column: gene_biotype
  aggregation: mode
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: gene_biotype
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: genes, by biotype

- component: card
  id: biotype_count
  title: Gene biotypes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct gene biotypes among the displayed genes and the ring splits the genes by biotype. It answers how varied the top genes are.
    How to read: a ring made of one large slice means the top genes are of one kind. Small slices are rare classes worth a look in the table.
  column: gene_biotype
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - mode
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: gene_biotype
  caption: genes, by biotype

- component: table
  title: Top gene counts
  description: |-
    Each row is one of the highest-count genes with its biotype and the Bambu count in every sample. It answers the exact counts behind the heatmap.
    How to read: sort a sample column to see its top genes and compare across columns.

- component: figure
  id: gene_expression_box
  title: Expression distribution per library
  description: |-
    Each box is the distribution of log2(CPM + 1) over the genes of one library, coloured by condition. It answers whether the libraries are comparable after normalising for depth.
    How to read: boxes of similar height and position mean comparable libraries. A library whose box sits well above or below its replicates has a composition or quality difference to check before comparing conditions.
    Lines and annotations: this catalog's recipe computes counts per million from the Bambu gene counts against the library total, then adds 1 before the log2 transform. The dashed line is the median log2(CPM + 1) of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Bambu.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoekeLab/bambu/master/README.md
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: log_cpm
    color: condition
    labels:
      sample: Library
      log_cpm: Expression, log2(CPM + 1)
      condition: Condition
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: log_cpm

- component: card
  id: log_cpm_spread
  title: Typical expression
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median log2(CPM + 1) over every gene and library in view, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers where expression typically sits.
    How to read: many genes are not detected in a library, so the median is low and the upper quartile is the more informative number. Filter to one condition to compare them.
  column: log_cpm
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median expression, with its spread

- component: card
  id: genes_by_biotype
  title: Genes quantified
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct genes, the compact line gives the gene and library rows, and the bars rank the biotypes by their genes. It answers how much of the annotation is covered and by what kind of gene.
    How to read: protein-coding genes usually lead. Rows divide by genes to give the number of libraries in view.
  column: gene_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: gene_biotype
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: genes, by biotype

- component: card
  id: reads_by_library
  title: Reads assigned
  description: |-
    The hero number is the sum of Bambu counts over the libraries in view, and the bars rank the libraries by their share. It answers how deep the sequencing is and how evenly it is spread.
    How to read: a library far below the others carries less information and its low counts are noisier. The compact line gives the median and maximum count of a single gene and library.
  column: count
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: reads, by library

- component: card
  id: biotype_rows
  title: Gene biotypes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct gene biotypes and the ring splits the gene and library rows by biotype. It answers what kinds of genes the table holds.
    How to read: one large slice is the usual protein-coding majority. The compact line gives the number of rows.
  column: gene_biotype
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: gene_biotype
  caption: gene rows, by biotype

- component: card
  id: cpm_peak
  title: Highest expression
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest counts per million of any gene in a library, and the bars rank the conditions by their top value. It answers whether one gene takes a large share of a library.
    How to read: a very high maximum means one gene dominates the library, which compresses the rest of the distribution. The compact line gives the median and the upper quartile.
  column: cpm
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - q3
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: condition
  top_n_count: 2
  caption: highest CPM, by condition

- component: table
  title: Gene counts per library
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene in one library with its biotype, Bambu count, counts per million and log2(CPM + 1). It answers the exact values behind the plots.
    How to read: filter to one library or condition and sort by counts per million to list the most expressed genes.
  page_size: 25

- component: advanced_viz
  id: top_expressed_transcripts_heatmap
  title: Most expressed transcripts by sample
  description: |-
    Each cell is the Bambu read count of one of the most highly counted transcripts (rows) in one sample (columns), scaled per transcript. It answers whether the highest-count isoforms behave the same in every library.
    How to read: columns of the same condition should share a pattern. A sample that looks unlike its replicates, or an isoform high in one condition only, is a candidate for isoform switching to follow up. Colour is a per-transcript z-score, so it shows the pattern across samples and not the absolute level.
    Lines and annotations: the transcripts are the 50 with the highest total count across samples, a fixed display size of this catalog's recipe and not a significance cut-off.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoekeLab/bambu/master/README.md
  kind: complex_heatmap
  config:
    normalize: row_z
  roles:
    index: transcript_id

- component: card
  id: transcripts_per_gene
  title: Genes behind the top transcripts
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct genes behind the displayed transcripts, the compact line gives the transcript count, and the bar shows the share of unique genes. It answers whether the top isoforms come from different genes.
    How to read: a unique share near the full bar means each top transcript belongs to its own gene. A lower share means several isoforms of one gene are among the most counted, which is where isoform usage deserves a look.
  column: gene_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: uniqueness
  caption: genes against transcripts

- component: table
  title: Top transcript counts
  description: |-
    Each row is one of the highest-count transcripts with its gene and the Bambu count in every sample. It answers the exact counts behind the heatmap.
    How to read: sort a sample column to see its top transcripts and compare across columns.

- component: figure
  id: isoform_expression_box
  title: Isoform expression distribution per library
  description: |-
    Each box is the distribution of log2(CPM + 1) over the transcripts of one library, coloured by condition. It answers whether the libraries are comparable after normalising for depth.
    How to read: boxes of similar height and position mean comparable libraries. A library whose box sits well above or below its replicates has a composition or quality difference to check before comparing conditions.
    Lines and annotations: this catalog's recipe computes counts per million from the Bambu transcript counts against the library total, then adds 1 before the log2 transform. The dashed line is the median log2(CPM + 1) of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Bambu.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoekeLab/bambu/master/README.md
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: log_cpm
    color: condition
    labels:
      sample: Library
      log_cpm: Expression, log2(CPM + 1)
      condition: Condition
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: log_cpm

- component: card
  id: isoform_log_cpm_spread
  title: Typical isoform expression
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median log2(CPM + 1) over every transcript and library in view, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers where isoform expression typically sits.
    How to read: most transcripts are not detected in a given library, so the median is low and the upper quartile is the more informative number. Filter to one condition to compare them.
  column: log_cpm
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median expression, with its spread

- component: card
  id: transcripts_by_biotype
  title: Transcripts quantified
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct transcripts, the compact line gives the transcript and library rows, and the bars rank the biotypes of their genes. It answers how much of the annotation is covered and by what kind of gene.
    How to read: protein-coding genes usually lead. Novel transcripts that Bambu discovered appear here as well.
  column: transcript_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: gene_biotype
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: transcripts, by biotype

- component: card
  id: genes_per_library
  title: Genes with isoforms
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct genes that have a quantified transcript, and the bars rank the libraries by the rows they hold. It answers how many genes the isoform table covers.
    How to read: libraries with fewer rows had fewer transcripts above the minimum count. Compare with the gene count of the gene-level table.
  column: gene_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: genes, by library

- component: card
  id: transcript_reads_by_condition
  title: Reads assigned
  description: |-
    The hero number is the sum of Bambu transcript counts over the libraries in view and the ring splits them by condition. It answers how the sequencing is shared between conditions.
    How to read: a lopsided ring means one condition has more reads, which counts per million correct for. The compact line gives the median and maximum count of a single transcript and library.
  column: count
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: condition
  caption: reads, by condition

- component: table
  title: Transcript counts per library
  description: |-
    Each row is a transcript in one library with its gene, biotype, Bambu count, counts per million and log2(CPM + 1). It answers the exact values behind the plots.
    How to read: filter to one library or gene and sort by counts per million to compare isoforms.
  page_size: 25

- component: advanced_viz
  id: correlation_heatmap
  title: Sample correlation
  description: |-
    Each cell is the Spearman correlation between two samples over their log2(CPM + 1) gene expression, with the condition as a row annotation and rows and columns clustered. It answers which samples resemble each other.
    How to read: replicates should form blocks of high correlation and conditions should separate. A sample that correlates better with the other condition, or with none, is a swapped label or a replicate that did not replicate.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is 1 by construction. Genes below a minimum total count are left out, and no correlation cut-off is applied.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: sample_id
    row_annotation_cols:
    - condition

- component: card
  id: mean_correlation_spread
  title: Mean correlation per sample
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average of each sample's mean correlation with the others, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how similar the libraries are overall.
    How to read: a high average with a tight box means a consistent run. A sample whose value sits far below the box is the outlier to inspect first. Rank correlation is high between any two samples of the same tissue, so compare samples within a run and not against an absolute value.
  column: mean_correlation
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mean correlation, with its spread

- component: card
  id: correlation_samples_by_condition
  title: Conditions and samples
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of conditions, the compact line gives the number of samples, and the ring splits the samples by condition. It answers how the run is balanced.
    How to read: unequal slices mean an unbalanced design, which weakens comparisons of the smaller group.
  column: condition
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: condition
  caption: samples, by condition

- component: table
  title: Sample correlation table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its condition, its mean correlation and its correlation with every other sample. It answers the exact values behind the heatmap.
    How to read: sort by mean correlation to find the least typical sample.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: pca
  title: Sample structure
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample placed by the first principal components of its log2(CPM + 1) gene expression, coloured by condition. It answers whether the samples group by condition.
    How to read: replicates of a condition should sit together and conditions should separate along the first component. A sample that sits with the wrong group or far from its replicates is an outlier or a swapped label, so check the correlation heatmap.
    Lines and annotations: the components use the 500 genes with the highest variance of log2(CPM + 1), the default number of genes of DESeq2 plotPCA.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thelovelab/DESeq2/devel/man/plotPCA.Rd
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: PC
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    dim_1: dim_1
    dim_2: dim_2
    dim_3: dim_3
    color: condition

- component: advanced_viz
  id: depth_vs_complexity
  title: Depth against genes detected
  description: |-
    Each point is a library: the reads Bambu assigned on the horizontal axis and the number of genes detected on the vertical axis, sized by the share of reads the 50 top genes take and coloured by condition. It answers whether depth explains how many genes were seen.
    How to read: genes detected rises with depth and then flattens. A library below its replicates at the same depth is less complex, and a large point means a few genes take much of the library. Both point to quality problems to check before comparing conditions.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median number of genes detected of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Bambu.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Reads assigned
    y_title: Genes detected
    top_n_labels: 6
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: total_counts
    y: n_genes_detected
    label: sample_id
    color: condition
    size: top50_share_pct

- component: figure
  id: reads_per_library
  title: Reads assigned per library
  description: |-
    Each bar is the number of reads Bambu assigned to genes in a library, coloured by condition. It answers how even the depth is across the run.
    How to read: bars of similar height mean comparable depth. A short bar is a library with little information, and counts per million correct for the difference only in part.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median reads assigned of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Bambu.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample_id
    y: total_counts
    color: condition
    labels:
      sample_id: Library
      total_counts: Reads assigned
      condition: Condition
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: total_counts

- component: card
  id: reads_by_condition
  title: Reads assigned
  description: |-
    The hero number is the sum of reads assigned over the libraries in view, and the bars rank the conditions by their share. It answers how much data the run holds and how it splits.
    How to read: a condition with far fewer reads is less well measured. The compact line gives the median and the largest library.
  column: total_counts
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: condition
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: reads, by condition

- component: card
  id: genes_detected_spread
  title: Genes detected
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of genes with reads per library, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how complex the libraries are.
    How to read: a tight box means similar complexity. A library far below it has lost genes to low depth or degradation.
  column: n_genes_detected
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median genes detected, with its spread

- component: card
  id: protein_coding_spread
  title: Protein-coding share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percentage of reads falling on protein-coding genes per library, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how clean the mRNA signal is.
    How to read: a library far below its replicates carries more ribosomal, mitochondrial or other RNA, which points to depletion or enrichment differences in the prep.
  column: pct_protein_coding
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median share, with its spread

- component: card
  id: top50_share_spread
  title: Share taken by the top genes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percentage of a library taken by its 50 most counted genes, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how concentrated expression is.
    How to read: a high share means a few genes use up the reads and leave less depth for the rest. A library above its replicates is more concentrated and less complex.
  column: top50_share_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median share, with its spread

- component: card
  id: samples_by_condition
  title: Conditions and samples
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of conditions, the compact line gives the number of samples, and the ring splits the samples by condition. It answers how the run is balanced.
    How to read: unequal slices mean an unbalanced design, which weakens comparisons of the smaller group.
  column: condition
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: condition
  caption: samples, by condition

- component: table
  title: Library readings
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its condition, the first three components, reads assigned, genes detected, protein-coding share and the share of the top 50 genes. It answers the exact values behind the plots.
    How to read: sort by reads assigned or genes detected to find the weakest libraries.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: variable_gene_heatmap
  title: Most variable genes
  description: |-
    Each cell is the log2(CPM + 1) expression of one of the most variable genes (rows) in one sample (columns), scaled per gene, with the gene biotype as a row annotation. It answers which genes drive the differences between samples.
    How to read: columns of the same condition should share a pattern. A sample that looks like the other group, or a block of genes that follows one condition, shows what structures the data before any contrast is run.
    Lines and annotations: the genes are the 100 with the highest variance of log2(CPM + 1) across the run, a fixed display size and not a significance cut-off. Colour is a per-gene z-score.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  config:
    normalize: row_z
  roles:
    index: gene_id
    row_annotation_cols:
    - gene_biotype

- component: card
  id: variance_spread
  title: Variance of the top genes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest variance of log2(CPM + 1) among the displayed genes, and the box shows the quartiles of all of them. It answers how strongly the top genes vary.
    How to read: a large maximum against a low box means a few genes carry most of the variation. High variance often marks genes that separate conditions, but also genes driven by one outlier library.
  column: log_cpm_variance
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: variance, with its spread

- component: card
  id: variable_biotypes
  title: Biotypes of the variable genes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct biotypes among the most variable genes, the compact line gives the most frequent one, and the bars rank the biotypes by gene count. It answers what kind of genes vary.
    How to read: mostly protein-coding genes is the usual picture. A non-coding class among them can be real regulation or a technical artefact.
  column: gene_biotype
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - mode
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: gene_biotype
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: genes, by biotype

- component: table
  title: Most variable genes table
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene with its biotype, the variance of its log2(CPM + 1) and its value in every sample. It answers the exact values behind the heatmap.
    How to read: sort by variance and compare a gene across the sample columns.
  page_size: 25
